newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM confirms Alitalia talks, says not firm.
newsitem.headline: KLM confirms Alitalia talks, says not firm.

text.p: Dutch carrier KLM Friday said it was in talks with Italy's Alitalia on a possible alliance, but played down reports they were at an advanced stage.

"(These talks) are contacts among the many under way now, in the past and in the future within the framework of everyone talking to everyone (in the industry)," KLM spokeswoman Marjolein Wenting said.
The Dutch newspaper NRC Handelsblad Friday quoted outgoing KLM President Pieter Bouw as saying the Dutch were firming up talks on a possible alliance with Alitalia.

The news about Alitalia came two days after KLM agreed to sell its 19 percent stake in Northwest Airlines back to the U.S. carrier for $1 billion in a deal meant to strengthen their lucrative but often stormy alliance.
Industry analysts said after that deal was announced on Wednesday that KLM's next priority would be to seek a European partner, and several of them said Alitalia was likely.
Speculation on a possible KLM-Alitalia tie-up has also grown after Spain's Iberia announced it was forging a link with British Airways.
Alitalia's state holding company IRI said this week that the airline was seeking an international alliance by the end of the year and named KLM as the prime contender.
